newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices ended a lackluster session unmoved, as scant new paper arrived and secondary issues continued to gather dust.
"The market is just really stale," a trader said, adding that retail interest remained slow and the market was tired of seeing the same names.
"We don't change levels," the trader said.
While 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds are slouching toward a 7.0 percent yield, munis are still trading not far from where they were when the bond was at a 6.75 percent or 6.80 percent yield, he said.

"We just don't follow well enough, and we have no supply pressure to really make us cheaper," the trader said. "Muni traders don't take hits unless they have to...Nobody buys, you can't get rid of what you own, you can't buy anything new at newer levels, so it's just pathetic."
Wednesday's actively quoted issues included Denver, Colo., City and County Airport 5.7 percent bonds of November 2025. The bonds were bid at 96-7/8, down from 97-1/4 at Tuesday's close.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond ended up 7/32 at 94-27/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 5/32 at 114-4/32. The March T-bond contract was up 6/32 at 110-8/32. The MOB spread was 124 ticks.

Turning to new issues, ABN AMRO Chicago Corp said it won $33 million Maryland National Park and Planning Commission bonds at a true interest cost of 5.3912 percent. Bonds were reoffered to investors at a top yield of 5.65 percent in 2017.
On the negotiated side, First Southwest Company tentatively priced $31 million Birdville Independent School District, Texas, bonds at a top yield of 5.60 percent in 2015 for the current coupon bonds.
